description.value: The study examined anticipatory somatosensory cortex activity during fear conditioning and its relationships with trait anxiety, auditory and amygdala activity, and whole-brain functional connectivity.

spans.text: As our main interests were how somatosensory processing during fear conditioning is modulated by trait anxiety during the perceptual processing and disambiguation of conditioned stimuli, and how such multisensory information is integrated, we estimated individuals’ BOLD signal during the CS tone interval.

design.value: A one-run fear-conditioning fMRI study using two conditioned tones, partial reinforcement with electric shock, ROI analyses, mediation analysis, and whole-brain functional connectivity and activation analyses.

spans.text: The conditioning task consisted of one run in which either the low- or high-pitched tone was paired with electric shock.
A total of 30 trials were presented in a random order: 10 CS+ with shock, 10 CS+ without shock and 10 CS− tones.
All participants completed the Spielberger State-Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI, [ 31 ]) before the fMRI scan.

description.value: A measure of individual differences in anxiety, including state and trait anxiety scores.

spans.text: The STAI is an established measure of individual differences in anxiety, which has also been widely used in the fMRI literature to measure the relationship between brain activity and individual differences in anxiety [ 32 , 33 , 34 , 35 ].

task_description.value: A tone discrimination fear-conditioning task with CS+ and CS− tones, partial reinforcement by mild electric shock, and button-press responses indicating whether the tone was low or high pitched.

spans.text: A total of 30 trials were presented in a random order: 10 CS+ with shock, 10 CS+ without shock and 10 CS− tones.
They were asked to indicate by button press with their index or middle finger of the right hand whether the tone was low or high pitched immediately after hearing the tone.
The conditioning task consisted of one run in which either the low- or high-pitched tone was paired with electric shock.
The schedule of stimulus presentation and data collection were controlled by the PsychToolbox extensions [ 36 , 37 ] based on Matlab 2010b (MathWorks Corp., Natrick, MA, USA).
